classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied warming model to verify the equation, calibrate k, evaluate temperature, invert for time and sketch the asymptote; each step is explicitly prompted.

content.prompt: A frozen casserole dish with initial temperature $T=0^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is left in an oven set to $180^\circ\mathrm{C}$. After ten minutes, the dish has temperature $T=30^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The rate that the temperature of the dish increases is proportional to the difference in temperature between the oven and the dish. Let $t$ be the time in minutes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Is the constant $k$ in parts b–d positive or negative?

answer.worked: The dish is warming, so $\dfrac{dT}{dt}>0$. Since $180-T>0$, the equation $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=k(180-T)$ requires $k>0$.
The temperature difference between the oven and the dish is $180-T$, so $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=k(180-T)$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that $T=180(1-e^{-kt})$ satisfies the differential equation from b.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}T&=180(1-e^{-kt})\\\frac{dT}{dt}&=180ke^{-kt}\end{aligned}$$
Substituting into the right-hand side:
$$\begin{aligned}k(180-T)&=k\bigl(180-180(1-e^{-kt})\bigr)\\&=k(180e^{-kt})\\&=180ke^{-kt}.\end{aligned}$$
Both sides are equal, so the model satisfies the differential equation.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the value of $k$. Leave in exact form.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find the temperature of the dish after an hour, to the nearest degree Celsius.

children.label: f
children.prompt: The dish is ready to serve when the interior temperature is at least $60^\circ\mathrm{C}$. After how many minutes, to the nearest minute, will the dish be ready?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}60&=180(1-e^{-kt})\\\frac13&=1-e^{-kt}\\e^{-kt}&=\frac23\\-kt&=\ln\!\left(\frac23\right)\\t&=\frac{\ln(3/2)}{k}\\&=\frac{10\ln(3/2)}{\ln(6/5)}\\&\approx22.239\text{ minutes}.\end{aligned}$$
The dish reaches $60^\circ\mathrm{C}$ after approximately $22.239$ minutes, which rounds to $22$ minutes. If checking only at whole minutes, the first ready time is $23$ minutes.

children.label: g
children.prompt: Draw a graph of the temperature against time, labelling all important features.

answer.short: An increasing, concave-down curve starting at $(0,0)$ and approaching the horizontal asymptote $T=180$.
answer.worked: $T(0)=0$, and $T\to180^\circ\mathrm{C}$ as $t\to\infty$. Since $T'(t)=180ke^{-kt}>0$ and $T''(t)=-180k^2e^{-kt}<0$, the graph increases at a decreasing rate.

spec.sourceRegion: Supplied answer graph beneath part g
spec.description: Positive arrowed time and temperature axes, increasing concave-down temperature curve from their intersection, and dashed horizontal limiting-temperature guide labelled 180. No grid or numerical time ticks.
